scorecard.rationale: The uncontrolled 14-person Parkinson brewed-green-tea pilot reports mean fatigue increasing from 28.4 to 32.1 and higher medians, with no paired variance or exact fatigue p value. Opposing evidence includes a postoperative whole-tea comparison and customary relief of tiredness. Some isolated caffeine and caffeine–theanine contrasts favor lower task fatigue. Controlled withdrawal comparisons suggest that short abstention can contribute to that signal. The usual-diet cycling outcome showed no caffeine condition effect and the taper trials do not report a separate fatigue contrast. The acute comparisons do not replicate a prepared green-tea Parkinson exposure. The closest pilot retains a tentative worsening lean. Controlled brewed-tea Parkinson results and the remaining original measures stay open.
